single.name: Single Card

positionNotes.focus: Read as a quality, feeling or perspective the card may bring to the question.

single.note: One card, read in depth for the question. With a yes-or-no or "should I" question, show what the card may bring to each side and leave the answer with the reader.

three_ppf.name: Past, Present, Future

positionNotes.past: Read as earlier influences, choices or habits that may still shape the situation.
positionNotes.present: Read as a mood, circumstance or inner stance that may be active now.
positionNotes.future: Read as a possible direction ahead.

three_ppf.note: One story in three steps: what may have shaped this, what may be active now, and a possible direction ahead. Offer the past and present as possibilities the reader may recognise, and keep the future card forward-looking with "may" and "if".

three_sao.name: Situation, Action, Outcome

positionNotes.situation: Read as circumstances, pressures and feelings that may surround the question.
positionNotes.action: Read as an approach or attitude the reader could weigh; describe what it may offer and ask.
positionNotes.outcome: Read as where that approach may lead.

three_sao.note: The action card is an approach the reader could weigh and the outcome card where it may lead, both in conditional wording ("if you…"). With a "should I" question, describe the approach and what it may ask, without endorsing or rejecting it.

relationship.name: Relationship

positionNotes.you: Read as what the reader may bring to the bond: feelings, needs, hopes and habits.
positionNotes.other: Read as how the reader may experience or see the other person, or what they might ask them about.
positionNotes.connection: Read as what the bond may share: common ground, dynamic and quality as the reader experiences it.
positionNotes.challenge: Read as a tension, difference or pattern that may strain the bond and could be looked at with care.
positionNotes.potential: Read as what the bond could grow into with care from both sides.

relationship.note: Any close bond counts: romantic, family, friendship or work. Read 'other' as how the reader may experience that person, never as their thoughts or intentions. If the question names no other person, read 'other' and 'connection' as the reader's close bonds in general and assume no partner; if the other person has died, as the reader's memory of them.

two_paths.name: Two Paths

positionNotes.situation: Read as the situation behind the choice: why it may matter now and what the reader may hope to find or protect.
positionNotes.path_a: Read as the first path (as the reader named it, or labelled by this card): what it might involve and ask for.
positionNotes.path_a_outcome: Read as where the first path may lead: what it may offer and what it may cost.
positionNotes.path_b: Read as the second path (as the reader named it, or labelled by this card): what it might involve and ask for.
positionNotes.path_b_outcome: Read as where the second path may lead: what it may offer and what it may cost.

two_paths.note: Path A is the first option the question names and path B the second. With no named options, call each path after its path card and describe it only through that card. Give both paths the same length and care: what each may offer and what each may ask.

celtic_cross.name: Celtic Cross

positionNotes.present: Read as the heart of the matter now.
positionNotes.challenge: Read as what crosses the situation: a tension that may need attention.
positionNotes.foundation: Read as the roots the situation may rest on.
positionNotes.recent_past: Read as recent influences that may still color things.
positionNotes.potential: Read as the hopeful aim the reader may be reaching for.
positionNotes.near_future: Read as what may come next if things continue as they are.
positionNotes.self: Read as the reader's own stance and strengths.
positionNotes.environment: Read as the people and circumstances around the reader, as the reader may experience them.
positionNotes.hopes_fears: Read as what the reader may hope for, fear, or both.
positionNotes.outcome: Read as the direction the cards may point to together.

celtic_cross.note: Keep each card section short and about its own card. The synthesis links present and challenge, the roots, self and environment, and hopes and fears flowing into the outcome.

phrases.noQuestion: The question is empty: name the main theme plainly in the overview's first sentence, then read what these cards invite the reader to notice in their life now, without inventing circumstances or mentioning the empty question.
phrases.withQuestion: Answer the question in the overview's first sentence, then tie every section to it and to the reader's own words.
phrases.regenerationIntro: The app rejected your previous attempt for this reason. Write a fresh reading that fixes it:
phrases.lengthFloor: Every range is a floor and a ceiling; keep sentences short.

ar.address: Write Modern Standard Arabic and address the reader in the second person singular, avoiding gender marking unless the question shows the reader's gender.

es.address: Address the reader informally with "tú", in gender-neutral wording.

fr.address: Address the reader with "vous", in gender-neutral wording.
fr.checkWords: "précis" / "précisément", "exact" / "exactement", "garanti", "sort" (also as "fate" and as the verb "il sort"), "guérir"

it.address: Address the reader informally with "tu", in gender-neutral wording.

ja.address: Write in polite です・ます form throughout.

pt.address: Address the reader with "você" (pt-BR), in gender-neutral wording.

uk.address: Address the reader formally with capitalised "Ви" (Вас, Вам, Ваш), in gender-neutral wording.
